summary: Ball became dead the instant it touched the grounded helmet — 5 penalty runs to the batting side.

steps.text: Ball, while in play, touches a fielding-side helmet resting on the ground.
Contact makes the ball dead immediately; 5 penalty runs are awarded to the batting side.
Because the ball was already dead, the subsequent take at slip cannot be a valid catch.

summary: A fair catch requires the ball not to have touched the ground since leaving the bat.

steps.text: For a catch to be fair, the ball must not have touched the ground after leaving the bat or glove.
Umpire judges the ball struck the pitch before reaching the fielder.
The take is not a valid catch, regardless of a clean take by the fielder.

summary: Given as Obstructing the Field — this used to be its own law before the 2017 Code folded it in.

steps.text: Batter wilfully fields the ball with a hand not currently holding the bat.
Done without the fielding side's consent, while the ball is in play.
Formerly its own law, "Handled the Ball" — merged into Obstructing the Field in the 2017 Code.

summary: Runs completed at the instant of the throw are added in full; the run in progress does not count.

steps.text: One run had been completed at the instant the throw was released.
The second run, only partway through, does not count as completed.
An overthrow reaching the boundary adds four runs on top of the completed total.
